parent_model_route.spend_authority_source: explicit user instruction, this conversation, dated by commit timestamp
parent_model_route.cost_boundedness_basis: The pinned dsh-agent-loop (packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts) nests two unbounded loops: turn() runs an outer `while (true)` over steps, and step() runs an inner `while (true)` per LLM request/retry. Neither loop has a native hard cap; a turn ends only when the model stops requesting tool calls (or errors/aborts), and a single turn may internally contain an arbitrary number of steps, each step being roughly one billed LLM call. A budget expressed only as a turn ceiling therefore does NOT bound total LLM call count or spend -- this was caught in this authorization's own hostile review (finding H-01) and fixed below by budgeting STEPS, not turns. A QntyLab-owned driver process (in the pattern of the existing pinned_dsh_codex_route_driver_v0.mjs) must externally enforce, by observing the session's own `step/start` events (the pinned loop already appends one per LLM call): (1) a hard maximum total-step count across the whole episode, (2) a hard wall-clock timeout, (3) a low llm-pi-ai retryPolicy.maxRetries ceiling, and (4) termination of the DSH process the instant the frozen step budget is reached. Under gpt-5-mini's worst-case per-call cost (128000 output tokens x $2/1e6 = $0.256), the frozen total-step ceiling below keeps worst-case spend under $1 with margin; this remains a conservative-implausibility bound enforced by the wrapper, not a framework guarantee, and is disclosed as such rather than overclaimed.
parent_model_route.max_output_tokens_override_mechanism: llm-pi-ai route model-catalog override (documented in packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/index.ts: a route's `models[].maxTokens` entry narrows the pi-ai catalog default for that model)
parent_model_route.retry_policy_h04_note: H-04 (pre-live, found and repaired on the execution branch before any live call): maxRetries was 2, not 0, at merge. step/start (packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts) fires once per step, BEFORE step()'s own internal retry loop, so a retry does not create a new step/start event -- a step-count-only guard undercounts request attempts. At maxRetries=2 one step could cost up to 3 attempts (24 across 8 steps), exceeding the $1.00 ceiling. maxRetries=0 makes 1 step == at most 1 request attempt, closing the gap monotonically (safety-restricting only; no other field changed).
parent_model_route.worst_case_single_call_cost_basis: (400000 input tokens x $0.25/1e6) + (4096 output tokens x $2/1e6) -- H-04's strengthened bound, using the model's full context window as the input assumption now that maxRetries=0 makes each step exactly one attempt; the model's raw catalog output cap (128000 tokens, $0.256/call) remains intentionally overridden downward rather than relied upon.

parent_lifecycle_budget.budget_unit_basis: One dsh-agent-loop turn may internally run an unbounded number of steps (packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts: turn()'s outer while(true) over steps has no framework cap); each step is approximately one billed LLM call. A turn-only ceiling does not bound spend, so the binding, externally-enforced control is a total STEP ceiling across the whole episode, inclusive of retries.
parent_lifecycle_budget.internal_parent_retries_disabled_h04_not: H-04 repair: maxRetries=0 (was 2) makes internal retries structurally absent rather than merely 'included' in the step count -- a step-count-only guard cannot see retries that happen inside step()'s own request loop without a new step/start event, so counting retries into the step budget was never actually enforceable; disabling them instead is the monotonic fix.
parent_lifecycle_budget.max_parent_request_attempts_basis: with internal_parent_retries_disabled, 1 step == at most 1 request attempt, so max_parent_request_attempts == parent_max_total_steps exactly
parent_lifecycle_budget.step_ceiling_enforcement_mechanism: external wrapper counts `step/start` session events (already emitted once per LLM call by the pinned loop) and hard-terminates the DSH process the instant parent_max_total_steps is reached, regardless of turn boundary; additionally asserts zero `llm/retry`/`llm/retry-started` events occur, since maxRetries=0 makes any such event an unexpected policy violation, not routine recovery
parent_lifecycle_budget.worst_case_episode_cost_basis: max_parent_request_attempts (8) x worst_case_single_call_cost_usd (0.108192, H-04-strengthened bound using the model's full 400000-token context window as the input assumption); margin under the $1.00 ceiling is approximately $0.134464

failure_taxonomy.PASS: Codex implementation passes all fixture tests unmodified; Claude's independent review finds no closure-blocking Critical/High; parent records PASS and stops.
failure_taxonomy.PASS_AFTER_BOUNDED_REPAIR: Claude's first review found a Critical/High; exactly one Codex repair call and one Claude targeted rereview occurred; rereview found none remaining; parent records PASS and stops.
failure_taxonomy.FAIL_IMPLEMENTATION: Codex's implementation (after any authorized repair) still fails one or more fixture tests.
failure_taxonomy.FAIL_REVIEW: Claude's review (after any authorized rereview) still finds an unresolved closure-blocking Critical/High.
failure_taxonomy.BLOCK_CHILD_INFRA: Codex or Claude Code native route failed to start, authenticate, or return a structured result for infrastructure reasons unrelated to the fixture task.
failure_taxonomy.BLOCK_PARENT_INFRA: The DSH parent process, build, or profile failed to start or run to a terminal turn for reasons unrelated to child task outcome.
failure_taxonomy.BLOCK_AUTH: A required native child credential or the parent OPENAI_API_KEY was absent, invalid, or rejected.
failure_taxonomy.BLOCK_COST: The frozen parent-step ceiling or wall-clock timeout was reached before a terminal outcome, or observed spend approached the $1 ceiling without a recorded result.
